history.dynasty: Chola (9th-century masonry core; Nandivarman Pallava renovated the sanctum; Rajendra I additions); inscriptions from Cholas, Pandyas, Nayaks and Marathas
history.period: 9th century CE core; expansions through the 16th century
history.summary: A major Paadal Petra Sthalam sung by Appar, Sundarar and Sambandar, and the chief of the Saptha Sthanam (seven Shiva temples of the region). Known as Dakshina Kailasam, it is held to be the birthplace of Nandi, Shiva's divine bull; Nandi's wedding with Suyasayambikai (celebrated at Thirumazhapadi) is commemorated in the annual Saptha Sthanam festival when the festival deity of Aiyarappar joins six others in decorated glass palanquins at Thillaistanam. 'Panchanadeeswarar' refers to the five rivers around the town (Arisilaaru, Vennaaru, Vettaaru, Kudamuruttiyaaru, Kaaviriyaaru). Legend: Karikala Chola's chariot stuck here, revealing buried idols and the meditating sage Niyamesar, who instructed the king to build the temple. CSV TOWN FLAG: town corrected from Thanjavur to Thiruvaiyaru (~13 km from Thanjavur).

name: Aiyarappar (Panchanadeeswarar) Temple
town_description: Thiruvaiyaru is a temple town in Thanjavur district about 13 km from Thanjavur, on the banks of the Cauvery. It is the heart of the Saptha Sthanam circuit of seven Shiva temples and the home of the annual Thyagaraja Aradhana music festival.

travel.airport: Tiruchirappalli International Airport, about 55-60 km away (verify).
travel.road: Well connected by road from Thanjavur (13 km) on the Thanjavur-Thiruvaiyaru route.

visitor_information.best_time: November to March; the Saptha Sthanam festival in Panguni (April) is the grandest occasion.
